source_name: CBCG — Javni registri i javne evidencije (public registers index, FOI section)
why_relevant: Statutory index of every public register and record CBCG maintains, published under the freedom-of-information regime — the most complete single enumeration of CBCG-held datasets, including ones not surfaced in the main navigation. Also the entry point for FOI (pristup informacijama) requests where data is not published.

source_name: CBCG — Priznate rejting agencije (recognised ECAIs)
why_relevant: Lists external credit assessment institutions recognised for capital-adequacy purposes — a pointer to third-party rating sources whose Montenegrin bank reports become an independent credibility cross-check.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (register of licensed banks)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to the full population of licensed banks (observed ~12 active: CKB, Hipotekarna, Prva banka, Erste, NLB, Addiko, Universal Capital Bank, Lovćen banka, Zapad banka, Ziraat Montenegro, Adriatic Bank, Podgorička banka). Each entry has its own sub-page with licence details and links onward to that bank's own IR/website — the seed list for every downstream actor-level crawl.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (payment institutions register)
why_relevant: Statutory register of licensed payment institutions and their agents under the Zakon o platnom prometu — the definitive map of non-bank PSP competition in Montenegro and a seed list for company-level tracking.

source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (e-money institutions register)
why_relevant: Definitive list of licensed e-money issuers and their agents — the fintech/EMI layer of the Montenegrin payments market.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (payment systems register)
why_relevant: Lists the payment systems authorised/operated in Montenegro (RTGS, DNS, and any card/instant schemes) — infrastructure-level map for payments market entry analysis.

source_name: CBCG — Pružaoci finansijskih usluga (leasing, faktoring, MFI, kreditno-garantni fondovi) registers
why_relevant: Registers and financial reports for non-bank credit providers (microcredit financial institutions, leasing, factoring, credit-guarantee funds) — adjacent supervised population that also buys banking/payments technology.

source_name: PKCG Odbor udruženja bankarstva, drugih finansijskih organizacija i osiguranja
why_relevant: Names ~23 member representatives spanning banks (Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, NLB, Prva, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat), insurers (Lovćen, Grawe, UNIQA), the central bank and development institutions, plus board officers (president Miloš Miketić - Lovćen banka; secretary Almer Bećiragić). Broader than UBCG because it includes insurance and non-bank finance.

source_name: PKCG Odbor udruženja informacionih i komunikacionih tehnologija (ICT board)
why_relevant: Chamber ICT board roster identifies the IT/payment-technology vendor population inside the formal chamber structure - relevant for the payments/fintech half of sector=both and for spotting POS/fiscalisation vendors.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Association of banking, other financial organisations and insurance
why_relevant: Chamber of Economy body that convenes sector events and is a named strategic partner of ME tech conferences; its event calendar and board composition point to which banks and vendors are organising sector gatherings.

entity_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore
source_name: Montenegro Stock Exchange (Montenegroberza) issuer pages for listed banks
why_relevant: Montenegrin banks are joint-stock companies (AD); the market-participant/issuer registry links per-bank issuer records and the disclosure filings that accompany shareholder assemblies, capital changes and ownership shifts — a route to bank disclosures that do not sit on the bank's own site.

source_name: Čikom d.o.o. (Podgorica) — ICT integrator, project/reference pages and LinkedIn feed
why_relevant: Čikom is described as a leading ME ICT company and digital-transformation integrator, appearing in national consortium projects (e.g. eKomora). Its reference/news output is a pointer to infrastructure and systems delivered into ME financial institutions.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (members, internships, open positions)
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 ME IT firms including Logate, which builds and maintains software systems for Montenegrin banks. Cluster member lists, aggregated open-position posts and its annual analysis of the top 30 ME IT companies map the domestic vendor bench that banks buy from, and hiring at those vendors is an even earlier signal than hiring at the banks.

source_name: ICT Cortex (Montenegrin ICT cluster) - members directory
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40+ Montenegrin tech companies including payments-relevant members (Payten, POS4, Coinis, Glovo, Telekom). It is the discovery index for payment-technology vendors and fintech-adjacent firms, and ICT Cortex co-organised the CBCG FinTech conference/hackathon with UBCG - a bridge between the tech and banking sides.

source_name: UBCG — Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (Association of Banks of Montenegro)
why_relevant: Industry body with all 11 ME banks as members; expanded remit into digitalisation/AI. Its statements and legislation section point to sector-wide positions on payment-scheme and SEPA implementation, and to member/bank actor lists.

source_name: UBCG member banks directory (11 licensed banks)
why_relevant: Enumerates the full population of licensed Montenegrin banks that are association members - Addiko, Adriatic, CKB (OTP), Erste, Hipotekarna, NLB, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad, Ziraat. Each entry snowballs into a bank IR/disclosure source for workstream A1.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — corporate registry mirror (Montenegroberza AD and issuers)
why_relevant: Commercial mirror of Montenegrin business-registry data (legal identity, address, activity code, financials) for the exchange itself and for listed issuers. Useful to resolve legal entity identity and detect name/status changes that precede or follow exchange announcements; it was the source that corrected the exchange's true domain (@mnse.me).

source_name: EMIS company profile - Erste Bank AD Podgorica (and peer Montenegrin subsidiaries)
why_relevant: Commercial database with standardised financials and executive data for Montenegrin bank subsidiaries; useful for entity identifiers and cross-checks, but subscription-gated.

source_name: Institut sertifikovanih računovođa Crne Gore (ISRCG)
why_relevant: IFAC full member since 2017; maintains registers of certified accountants/auditors and publishes professional guidance. Its member registers point to the audit firms that sign Montenegrin bank annual reports - a useful bridge into A1 disclosure sources.

source_name: Zakon o reviziji + registar ovlašćenih revizora i revizorskih društava
why_relevant: Defines the statutory audit register and which entities must file audited accounts. The auditor register is itself an actor map (Big-4 vs local firms auditing ME banks and PSPs) and a snowball source for audited-entity lists.

source_name: MFIC Banking Committee
why_relevant: MFIC's Banking Committee is the coordination platform for foreign-owned banks in Montenegro; its membership is effectively a directory of the foreign-owned bank population and its output feeds White Book banking chapters.

source_name: SeeCapitalMarkets — SEE exchange aggregator (Montenegroberza pages)
why_relevant: Regional South-East-Europe capital-markets aggregator with a Montenegroberza section; useful as a cross-market pointer for comparing ME listed-bank disclosure practice with RS/HR/BA peers and for discovering additional data endpoints.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer databases (Diebold Nixdorf, Oracle FLEXCUBE, etc.)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that compiles vendor customer lists per product. Useful as a cross-check index to test whether any ME bank appears against core-banking / self-service products, and to generate candidate vendor-bank pairs for targeted verification.

source_name: CompanyData.com — Montenegro legal-entity database (CRPS-derived bulk)
why_relevant: Vendor offering ~92k ME legal entities sourced from CRPS via API/CSV with 50+ fields including corporate ownership. Candidate for one-shot bulk acquisition of the entity spine instead of scraping the registry.

source_name: ecoi.net – archived copies of EU and Council of Europe country documents on Montenegro
why_relevant: Independent mirror/archive of enlargement-package SWDs and related assessments with stable document IDs; useful fallback when Commission download links rotate, and a convenient way to enumerate document history.

source_name: eUprava Crne Gore (e-government service portal)
why_relevant: Directory of official electronic services incl. CRPS registry and financial-statement filing/access services; pointer to where structured company data actually lives.

source_name: FinancialReports.eu - filings index for NLB Banka AD / Asseco SEE and other parents
why_relevant: Indexes issuer filings across EU venues; a convenient discovery layer for locating group annual/interim reports and their attachments when issuer sites reorganise URLs.

source_name: Halcom — list of banks using Halcom (e-banking client index)
why_relevant: Halcom publishes an explicit, maintained list of banks running its Hal E-Bank corporate e-banking and qualified-certificate stack across the ex-YU region. Where Montenegrin banks appear, this is a direct vendor-confirmed client mapping for corporate digital channels.

source_name: IT klaster Crne Gore (ITCMNE)
why_relevant: Second, older (est. 2013) Montenegrin IT cluster focused on e-gov applications and cross-industry services; a complementary member directory to ICT Cortex for identifying vendors that build payment/e-service infrastructure.

source_name: Media Ownership Monitor Montenegro
why_relevant: Not a news source but the authoritative registry of Montenegrin outlets with ownership structures and shareholding percentages (e.g. Monitor d.o.o. majority-held by the Perović family at 51.83%). Essential for scoring the credibility and political alignment of every other source in this cell, and for discovering outlets not surfaced by search.

source_name: Nacionalni biro osiguravača Crne Gore (NBOCG) - National Bureau of Insurers
why_relevant: Statutory association of insurers (6 member organisations) handling Green Card and compulsory motor insurance; a member directory plus claims/payout statistics for the insurance half of sector=both, and a counterpart body to UBCG.

source_name: NVOinfo.me - Montenegrin NGO/association registry entries
why_relevant: Registry-style directory confirming legal identity, registration date (UBCG registered 2003-04-07), address and contact of associations. Useful for verifying that an 'association' is a real registered entity and for discovering further sector NGOs/associations by keyword.

source_name: Softing d.o.o. (ME) — eCommerce integrations page (payment-gateway/acquirer integration list)
why_relevant: A Montenegrin software house publishing which bank e-commerce gateways it integrates with. Vendor-side integration lists reveal which acquiring banks and which gateway platforms are live in ME — a rare, concrete acceptance-side pointer.

source_name: Tracxn — FinTech startups in Montenegro (company database)
why_relevant: Aggregator listing ~102 Montenegro-registered fintech entities with funding status (10 funded, 1 Series A+) — including forex/crypto entities (AMarkets, GoDefi, Impact, Prosecure, GANNMarkets). Useful for actor discovery, but note many are foreign-founded entities domiciled in ME rather than domestic payment challengers.

source_name: Wikipedia — List of banks in Montenegro (actor-map pointer)
why_relevant: Fast actor-map scaffold enumerating licensed Montenegrin banks (CKB, NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna, Prva banka Crne Gore, Erste, Lovćen, Adriatic/First Financial, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Razvojna banka) with parent-group links. Use only to generate the search-term list; the authoritative register is CBCG's own bank list, and Wikipedia entries can be stale.
